text:
Priya R: Quick RFC follow-up — I want to propose pulling tenant affinity (sticky routing / 'affinity tokens') out of session-mesh and into its own tiny service (affinity-service). RFC: https://redwood.internal/rfc/affinity-demux (summary below).

Mike L: Why? session-mesh already handles this today, right?

Priya R: Yeah. Main reasons: 1) session-mesh is huge and hot-path — complexity correlates with frequent deploy churn, 2) multiple runtimes want the same affinity semantics (runtime A, runtime B, Dedicated), 3) decoupling will let us optimize caching + eviction policies separately.

Sasha: Latency impact concerns — adding a hop could regress p50. Have numbers?

Priya R: Good point. Goal: keep single-hop by co-locating affinity-service as a sidecar in hotpaths or as in-process lib for runtimes that prefer it. We measured a prototype: local sidecar median add ~350us, net effect on token-path p50 is ~1% in synthetic. We can also inline a fast local cache in the mesh to avoid remote calls for hit cases.

Andre: How would the interface look? Simple header? Token?

Priya R: Minimal API: request -> returns affinity token + route info. Fallback semantics: if affinity-service unreachable, fall back to session-mesh soft-affinity (best-effort). Example header we propose: X-Affinity-Token: <base64>. Docs snippet: 
```
GET /v1/affinity?tenant_id=acme-1&trace_id=...
200 {"token":"ABCD..","node":"node-42","expires_at":"1680000000"}
```
Or runtime can call local lib: affinity.lookup(tenant, key) -> token.

Leah: Data ownership: where does the KV live? Is this another durable store?

Priya R: We plan 3 tiers: memory-first LRU cache in each sidecar, replicated delta-store (Raft) for small active sets (per-region), and optional durable backing (Postgres) for cold state. Active affinity entries are tiny so Raft per-region looks fine.

Mike L: Migration story? We can't break existing long-lived sessions.

Priya R: Migration plan in RFC summary: 
1) Build affinity-service and a read-only shadow mode in session-mesh (session-mesh queries new service but continues own writes).
2) Run shadow for 2 weeks, compare token mappings, assert parity > 99.99%.
3) Flip to read-write in session-mesh but with a canary header: X-Affinity-Source: affinity-service for 10% of tenants. Monitor error/latency regressions and routing divergence.
4) Full cutover and then remove old session-mesh affinity code.

Sasha: What about cache consistency edge cases — e.g., eviction race where token moves and request hits stale node?

Priya R: We'll introduce generation numbers in tokens and short TTLs (30s default). On divergence, the router falls back to deterministic hashing (stateless), and we surface a metric affinity.divergence.count. Also a reconciliation job runs every 15m to resolve hot-key thrashing.

Andre: Rollback plan?

Priya R: Rollback: switch session-mesh back to its internal store (we'll keep feature-flag toggles). If affinity-service causes instability, we can route reads back to session-mesh and stop writes. Documented runbook in RFC: runbook snippet below.

Leah: SLOs/metrics we need to track?

Priya R: Agreed. Minimum: affinity.latency.p50/p95, affinity.error_rate, affinity.cache_hit_ratio, affinity.token_mismatch_rate, routing.fallback_rate. We'll also create a dashboard that annotates canary tenants.

Mike L: Any security concerns with tokens in headers? token forgery?

Priya R: Tokens are HMAC-signed with region key and include short TTL + generation. No PII in token. For private deployments, customers can bring KMS keys.

Sasha: Testing: unit + integration + a chaos test that kills affinity-service pods mid-request?

Priya R: Yes. Add chaos tests: pod kill, network partition, raft leader stepdown. Also load tests with realistic tenant skew (Zipf) to ensure hot-key handling.

Andre: Ownership and maintenance — which team will own this?

Priya R: Proposal: Eng-Runtime owns the service for the first 6 months, then rotate to a service-owner in Platform if it's broadly used. We'll add a quarterly review.

Leah: Are we adding new deploy surface for Private (on-prem) customers?

Priya R: Provide two install modes: embedded (as a library compiled into on-prem runtime) and standalone service (K8s manifest + helm chart). Private customers can choose.

deploy-bot: Deployed prototype to staging: affinity-service:v0.1 (link: https://staging.deps/affinity/v0.1). Canary set created for tenant group 'alpha'.

Mike L: Nice. Next actions?

Priya R: I'll open a tracking epic with tasks: infra/helm, Raft store spike, sidecar integration, shadow-mode PR for session-mesh, e2e tests, dashboard + alerts. Will post links later. If there are no blocking objections, I'd like to start the spike tomorrow.

Sasha: +1 from me, please add a small perf budget and ensure we can fallback to deterministic hash without config changes.

Andre: +1, also add a migration postmortem checklist to the epic.

Leah: +1, please include a privacy review for token payloads.

Priya R: Thanks all. Will create the epic and ping in #eng-release when ready. :raised_hands:
